body:
Triage: `pm:blocked` + `domain:devx`, Task, S — prose-accuracy fix in `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs`, correctly deferred behind the constant's actual removal.

Blocked-by: #11930

Ordering update since filing: the card's second ordering leg is discharged — **PR #12061 will not land** (the #11935 retriage upheld the 2026-08-23 adjudication and closed that card as a duplicate; the draft PR is to be closed unmerged by the devx seat). So the only live upstream is #11930's PR removing `GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS`; when the unlock scan returns this card, re-check on the merged ref whether that PR already amended the `why` sentence before dispatching a one-line edit.

## Unlocked, verified, and claimed — `pm:blocked` → `pm:dispatched`

Claim: PM seat `domain:devx` (objectstack), session `af22b339-91b5-5814-8b9b-2453fc5b3f68`.

- **Branch:** `claude/issue-12095-stale-generated-skill-artifacts-ref`
- **Worktree:** dedicated per-task worktree off a fetched `origin/main` (Prime Directive #11)
- **Declared file surface:** `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` — **one string, line ~715**. Nothing else.
- **Model tier:** opus. No path-derived mandate. Tier chosen against the *bottleneck*, not the diff: the merge queue is the constraint right now (5-wide, rebuilds every resident entry on each merge), so a cycle lost to a sloppy verification section costs more than the tier does. The edit is trivial; the surrounding contract is not.
- **Clause ② (contract review):** no. Prose accuracy inside a gate's `why` record.
- **Serial constraints:** ⭐ **now none** — see below.

### Both `Blocked-by` conditions have resolved, in opposite ways

The card's ordering clause said this should ride whichever landed **second** of #11930's PR and #12061.

- **#12061 — closed WITHOUT merging** (12:10Z). So it will never rewrite this entry, and the card's own escape hatch — *"If #12061 rewrites that entry wholesale, check whether this is already moot"* — is **void**, not satisfied. Nothing was rewritten. `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` is now unclaimed.
- **#11930's PR merged** as **#12097** (`71f9cd1d75`), which removed `GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS`.

### Premise re-verified on the merged ref — and it is now sharper than when filed

Upstream landing is not the same as the card still standing, so I measured rather than inferred:

```
$ git grep -c 'GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS' origin/main -- scripts/ packages/
origin/main:scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs:1        ← the ONLY hit anywhere

$ git grep -c 'SKIP_PATHS' origin/main -- scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs
origin/main:scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs:1        ← positive control

$ git show origin/main:scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs | grep -n GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS
715:    why: 'Carries no ratchet at all. ROOTS, SKIP_PATHS, SKIP_FILES and GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS are declarations of …'
```

**The constant is gone from the entire tree. Its single surviving mention is this prose string.** When the card was filed the removal was still in flight; it has now landed, so the reference is unambiguously stale rather than prospectively so. The card got *easier* while it waited, which is the good case for a `Blocked-by` hold.

### Zone 1 — rulings, not renegotiable

1. **Drop `GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS` from that sentence and nothing else.** The remaining names (`ROOTS`, `SKIP_PATHS`, `SKIP_FILES`) are live — verified above for one of them, verify the rest yourself.
2. **⛔ Do not touch the closing line.** *"Its published-catalog id rule reached this corpus by first shipping a per-passage allowlist and being turned red here for offering it … If this flips, that list came back."* That is about the **per-passage allowlist**, a different thing, and the card says explicitly it is unaffected. It also encodes a maintainer ruling of 2026-08-25. Leave it byte-identical.
3. **⛔ Do not "fix" anything else in this file.** It carries other entries and other `why` records. This is a one-string card; anything else you notice gets filed.

### Zone 2 — falsify, do not inherit

- I assume the grammar reads correctly after removing the fourth item from a four-item list (`A, B, C and D` → `A, B and C`). Read the resulting sentence; if it needs a comma or conjunction change to stay grammatical, that is in scope.
- I assume **nothing parses this string**. The card asserts it (*"nothing parses the `why` string against the file"*) and the gate stayed green through #12097 with the string already stale, which is consistent. **Confirm it anyway** — if some self-test or sibling gate matches on the `why` text, this edit reds it and that changes the card.
- I assume `ROOTS` and `SKIP_FILES` are still live in this file. I verified `SKIP_PATHS` only. Check all three; if another has also been removed, that is a second instance of the same defect and belongs in the same PR.

### Zone 3 — suggested route

Read the entry whole before editing, confirm the other three names resolve, make the one-string change, run the derived gate union. **No ablation applies** — a comment/record string with no execution path has nothing to mutate, and claiming one would be theatre. Say that rather than inventing a leg. Changeset: root `scripts/` only, no published-package source change ⇒ `skip-changeset`.

Report per the os-dev contract. Out-of-scope findings get filed, not fixed.

## PM review — ACCEPT (landing blocked on `main`, not on this PR)

Reviewed PR #12187 against the dispatch. One file, `+1/−1`, `size/xs`. Accepted — and it exposes a circular control in my own dispatch.

### ⭐ My positive control was circular, and this PR's method is what shows it

In the dispatch I wrote:

> I verified `SKIP_PATHS` only. Check `ROOTS` and `SKIP_FILES` too.

What I actually ran was:

```
git grep -c 'SKIP_PATHS' origin/main -- scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs   → 1
```

**That `1` is the `why` string itself** — the very prose I was asking to have edited. `check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` does not *define* `SKIP_PATHS`; it only *mentions* it, inside the sentence under repair. So my "verification that SKIP_PATHS is live" verified nothing except that the sentence exists. Had all four names been dead, my grep would have returned `1` for every one of them and I would have reported them all live.

The PR gets it right, and says why in a sentence I want on the record:

> They describe constants in `scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs`, so that is where liveness was measured — **not in the file carrying the prose, where a grep only ever re-finds the sentence itself.**

Measured in the correct file, with definitions located:

```
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:93   const ROOTS = ['.claude', 'docs', 'skills', 'content'];
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:123  const SKIP_PATHS = new Set([
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:130  const SKIP_FILES = new Set(['content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx']);

occurrences: ROOTS 26 · SKIP_PATHS 12 · SKIP_FILES 3 · GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS 0
```

That establishes both halves at once: the three survivors are live, and the fourth is a single instance rather than one of several.

⇒ **Seat error (13), and it is the same family as (11).** On #12052 I ran a control with a *narrower pattern* than the measurement; here I ran one against the *wrong file*, where it could only ever confirm itself. Both are controls that validate something other than the thing being measured. The sharpened rule: **a positive control must be capable of returning a different answer than the measurement.** If it cannot fail independently, it is decoration. That is now five of thirteen seat errors in the "partial or circular reading presented as complete" family — comfortably the dominant one.

### The rest of the brief, checked

**Zone 1 ruling 1 — one name, and the grammar handled.** `ROOTS, SKIP_PATHS, SKIP_FILES and GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS` → `ROOTS, SKIP_PATHS and SKIP_FILES`; the conjunction moves so the four-item list does not leave a dangling `and`. That was the Zone 2 grammar point and it was applied rather than noted.

**Zone 1 ruling 2 — the closing sentence is byte-identical**, verified by comparing the tail segment against `origin/main` (267 bytes on both sides) rather than by eye. That sentence carries a maintainer ruling of 2026-08-25, so "looks unchanged" would not have been good enough.

**Zone 1 ruling 3 — no other entry or `why` record touched.** One file, one line.

**Zone 2 — "nothing parses the `why` string" — answered properly, not assumed.** `declared.why` has exactly one consumer: line 826, interpolated into the `MISCLASSIFIED:` failure text. Never matched, split, or compared. No file reads this gate as text; the four other referrers of the filename name it only in comments, a message string, and the npm script that invokes it. The gate's own `--self-test` pins no entry text. And that is consistent with the observable fact that the gate stayed green through #12097 while the string was already stale — a prediction the evidence had to match, and does.

**No ablation, stated as such.** *"A record string with no execution path has nothing to mutate — there is no leg here that could be made to fail, and constructing one would be theatre rather than evidence."* Correct, and said out loud rather than silently omitted.

### ⛔ Landing is blocked, and not by this PR

This PR is based on `22c42c9b21`, which is the poisoned `main`: `check:exported-any-returns` fails there on a stale `packages/client` ledger row that PR #12062 closed the gap for but never deleted. So `Type Check · consumer gates` will go red on this PR for a reason that has nothing to do with a one-word prose edit in a `scripts/` gate.

⛔ **Nothing will be pushed here for that.** Filed already by two other seats as **#12180** and **#12184**, both dispatched; `packages/client` is `domain:cli`'s surface. This PR waits for `main` to recover and then lands unchanged.

Landing condition once `main` is green: every named gate job `completed` + `success`. `Lint & Repo Gates` carries `check:ratchet-remedy-authority` — the gate this diff edits — so that is the one that decides here.

## Zone 2 — all three assumptions checked, one of them was wrong

**1. Grammar — the PM's assumption held, but the edit is NOT a pure deletion.** Removing the fourth item of `A, B, C and D` leaves a dangling `and`, so the conjunction had to move: the substitution is `ROOTS, SKIP_PATHS, SKIP_FILES and GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS are` → `ROOTS, SKIP_PATHS and SKIP_FILES are`. This was explicitly in scope per Zone 2. Plural agreement (`are declarations`, `each is path-scoped`) is unchanged with three items.

**2. Nothing parses the `why` string — confirmed, not inherited.** `declared.why` has exactly one consumer in the whole gate: line 826, `control's reason: ${declared.why}`, interpolated into the `MISCLASSIFIED:` failure text. It is never matched, split, compared, or hashed. No file in the repo reads `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` as text — the four other referrers of that filename (`package.json`, `check-doc-authoring.mjs`, `check-auth-mount-ledger.mjs`, `check-i18n-coverage.mjs`) name it only in prose comments, one message string, and the npm script that invokes it. `check-doc-authoring.mjs` appears exactly once in the gate: at line 713, the CONTROL key itself. No self-test pins entry text. The gate's own run above is the live confirmation.

**3. `ROOTS` and `SKIP_FILES` — live. There is no second instance of the defect.** Measured where the constants actually are (`scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs`), not in the file carrying the prose:

```
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:93:  const ROOTS = ['.claude', 'docs', 'skills', 'content'];
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:123: const SKIP_PATHS = new Set([
scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs:130: const SKIP_FILES = new Set(['content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx']);

occurrences in that file:  ROOTS 26 · SKIP_PATHS 12 · SKIP_FILES 3 · GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS 0
```

One note on method, offered because it would matter on a card where the answer differed. The claim comment's positive control — `git grep -c 'SKIP_PATHS' -- scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs → 1` — cannot distinguish a live constant from a stale one: the single hit it returns **is the prose sentence under repair**. `GENERATED_SKILL_ARTIFACTS` scores exactly `1` on that same control. The discriminating measurement is the one above, against the file that declares the names. It happened to agree here.
